answer: A beacon registry can resist sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake before its beacon identity is listed. New identities start in a nebula of untrusted newcomers with limited quotas, and only earn full trust after sustained honest work verified by peers. Like a cedar that takes years to grow tall, reputation accrues slowly but can be slashed instantly for fraud. An attacker must therefore pay a separate stake and waiting cost for every fake identity, making large-scale fakery expensive while honest agents pay almost nothing beyond good behavior.
